title: BIMSTEC: The Bay of Bengal Club

segments.say: Around one sea, the Bay of Bengal, live more than a fifth of the world's people. In nineteen ninety-seven, the countries on its shores formed a club.

anim.title: Seven members
items: South Asia: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka

segments.say: It's called BIMSTEC, and it has seven members: five from South Asia, and two from South-East Asia, Myanmar and Thailand.
The name is a mouthful: the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation.

items.text: Nepal and Bhutan join; seven members

segments.say: It began in Bangkok with four members, grew to seven by two thousand four, set up its office in Dhaka in twenty fourteen, and signed a charter in twenty twenty-two.
For India, BIMSTEC is a bridge from South Asia to South-East Asia, joining its 'Neighbourhood First' and 'Act East' policies, at a time when SAARC has often been stalled.
The work is shared out by sector: trade, energy, transport, security, fisheries and more. The weak spot: trade deals have taken years and are still being negotiated.

anim.title: For your answer
items: Link between Neighbourhood First and Act East

segments.say: For GS Two: BIMSTEC, nineteen ninety-seven, seven members, office in Dhaka, India's bridge to the east.
